label: Brent Crude
value: $101.61/bbl Sep 21 (9:35am ET, -$2.72), down further from the $104.33 Sep 18 close after a new Hormuz tanker strike and a weekend transit collapse
delta: Fell further Sep 21 as shipping data showed just 17 commodity vessels transited Hormuz over the weekend, down from 37 the week before, even as a fresh unidentified-projectile strike hit an inbound tanker in the strait Monday

label: Saudi East-West Pipeline
value: Shut since Sep 11; Yanbu Red Sea loadings also suspended Sep 15 (~4-5M bpd, 4-5% of global supply); Saudi signals ~half capacity restorable within days, full repair up to 6 weeks
source: The Times of Israel / Business Recorder / CNBC / Kpler (Sep 15-17, 2026)
contestNote: US Energy Secretary Chris Wright says the outage will be 'measured in days'; UK officials and some industry sources cite repair estimates of five to six weeks; Kpler expects only a partial bypass restoring about half of exports within a month
delta: Aramco suspended crude loadings at Yanbu and cancelled some September cargoes to European customers; total Saudi crude loadings have fallen over 70% (7.5M bpd Jan-Feb to 2.1-2.3M bpd mid-Sep) as exports reroute via Sohar ship-to-ship transfers, the Suez/Sumed pipeline and the Cape of Good Hope

label: Saudi Crude Loadings vs. Pre-Crisis
delta: Replacement flow moving via Sohar ship-to-ship transfers and the Strait of Hormuz itself (2M+ bpd), a smaller volume via Suez/Sumed, and limited use of the much longer Cape of Good Hope route

label: Bab el-Mandeb Daily Transits
delta: New second chokepoint risk: Houthi capture of Yemen's Mokha port and advance toward the strait cut Red Sea vessel crossings from 30 (Wed) to 12 (Thu), narrowing the Suez/Red Sea bypass route shippers have used to avoid the closed Strait of Hormuz

label: US Diesel Price
delta: Crossed $6/gallon for the first time as the Sep 9-10 shipping-attack wave and the new Red Sea front pushed Brent toward its $108 crisis peak

label: FAO Food Price Index
source: FAO (Aug 2026, released Sep 4 -- highest since late 2022)
delta: Up 1.9% from July's revised level and 2.5% y/y; broad-based across all five commodity groups -- sugar +11.9% m/m, cereals +2.2% m/m (highest since May 2024), dairy +2.3% m/m

label: Hormuz Daily Tanker Transits
value: 17 vessels over the Sep 19-20 weekend (down from 37 the week before) vs ~10M bbl/day and a 'six-month high' claimed (US)
source: Reuters / Kpler via KELO / US News (Sep 20-21, 2026)
contestNote: CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper said oil and LNG shipments through the strait hit a six-month high over the preceding two weeks, topping 1 billion barrels; independent Kpler-based tracking counted just 17 trackable commodity vessels crossing over the Sep 19-20 weekend, down from 37 the prior weekend, against a pre-war daily average of roughly 125 large commercial vessels
delta: vs 3 vessels on Sep 17 (single-day record low) and 130-140/day (100+ ships) pre-war
deltaNote: Weekend count roughly halved week-on-week even as the US cites a six-month shipment high; Middle Eastern producers continue exporting on tankers with transponders disabled, which trackable counts miss
